description: What: one timeline of a CCE performance test: what k6 sent (rate, latency, errors, dropped iterations) next to the collector, matcher and Step SLA counters, Kafka lag, DB pools, JVM, container CPU/memory, disk and Postgres WAL / replication slots. How: provisioned by monitoring/docker-compose.yml (http://localhost:3030) or imported into CCE's Grafana (monitoring/cce-grafana-import/README.md); pick the run in "Run id". Needs: a Prometheus datasource (DS_PROMETHEUS) holding k6 remote-write series (labels testid, service, test_type) and the scrape jobs of monitoring/prometheus/prometheus.yml. Outputs: nothing written; panels and run annotations only.

panels.description: Orientation for newcomers: which rows are filtered by the run and which are not.

options.content: Top rows: what **k6 sent** (filtered by *Run id*, *Service*, *Test type*). Lower rows: what the **services, Kafka, Postgres, containers and disk** did (not filtered: use the time range). The shaded region is a k6 run; green markers are the test runner's phase/"started breaking" annotations (tags `cce-performance` + run id). Step SLA runs have no k6 metrics: type the run id in *Run id*. Per-service detail: see the *CCE Performance dashboards* links (top right).

panels.title: How to read this dashboard
Load sent by k6 (filtered by Run id, Service, Test type)

panels.description: How many HTTP requests k6 STARTED per second (k6 counter http_reqs, pushed by remote write). Tests use an open model: k6 starts requests at the configured arrival rate whether or not the service keeps up, so this line should be flat at the target rate. A dip below the target means k6 could not start requests on time (see dropped iterations). Empty for matcher and Step SLA tests (they send no HTTP).
panels.title: k6 HTTP requests per second (collector tests)

panels.description: How many events k6 wrote to the Kafka topic cce.events.inbound per second (xk6-kafka writer counter). Empty for collector and Step SLA tests. If empty during a matcher test, check the metric name at first scrape (k6_kafka_writer_message_count_total).
panels.title: k6 Kafka messages per second (matcher tests)

panels.description: Time from k6 sending a request to receiving the full response, as seen by k6. p95 = 95 % of requests were faster than this. k6 exports these in SECONDS (multiplied by 1000 here) and calculates them from its own samples, so they can lag behind a sudden change; the run report's per-window numbers are the reference. Dashed line: the default pass limit HTTP_P95_LIMIT_MS = 500 ms (to be confirmed from UAT/Dev data; a run may override it). Only the collector has server-side times, and only avg/max (no histogram buckets exported).
panels.title: k6 HTTP latency p95 / p99 (ms)

panels.description: Share of HTTP requests that failed (k6 marks a response as failed when its status is not expected, or on a time-out / connection error). "last 30 s" is calculated from the request counter and reacts quickly; "whole run so far" is k6's own http_req_failed rate. Dashed line: HTTP_MAX_FAILED_RATE = 1 % (to be confirmed).
panels.title: k6 failed requests (share)

panels.description: Iterations k6 should have started (open model) but could not, because all its virtual users were busy. A few are tolerated (MAX_DROPPED_RATE = 0.1 % of planned events, to be confirmed by the team). Many dropped iterations with LOW latency mean k6 itself is the limit ("at least X/s, k6 limit"), not the service; with HIGH latency the service is slow and k6 ran out of VUs waiting for it.
panels.title: k6 dropped iterations per minute

panels.description: Virtual users k6 has allocated to keep up with the arrival rate. In an open model this grows when responses get slower (each VU waits for its response). Reaching the scenario's maxVUs means the next iterations are dropped.
panels.title: k6 virtual users (VUs)
What the services did (not filtered by run: use the time range and the run markers)

panels.description: Events the collector accepted (HTTP 202 and stored in inbound_event_log), from its own counter. During a collector test this should follow the k6 request rate; a gap means requests failed or were rejected. Service metrics carry no run id: use the time range and the run markers to find your run.
panels.title: Collector: accepted events per second

panels.description: Events the matcher finished (matched at least one plan-definition trigger, or matched none), from its counter cce_events_matched_total. When this stays below the arrival rate, the backlog grows. Service metrics carry no run id: use the time range and the run markers to find your run.
panels.title: Matcher: processed events per second

panels.description: Events waiting in the topic cce.events.inbound that the matcher's consumer group has not read yet (from kafka-exporter). It should return to 0 after sending stops; the time it takes is the catch-up time. Dashed line: MATCHER_MAX_BACKLOG = 1,000 (to be confirmed).
panels.title: Matcher backlog (Kafka consumer lag)

panels.description: SLA transition rows ("alarms") whose time has come and that the next Step SLA cycle would fetch (gauge cce_sla_transitions_due; the service runs a SQL count for every scrape). It should return to near 0 within a few poll intervals; a value that keeps growing means Step SLA cannot keep up.
panels.title: Step SLA: alarms due now
JVM and database pool (collector, matcher, Step SLA)

panels.description: Threads waiting for a database connection, per service. Above 0 = the pool is exhausted: work queues before it can touch the database (the collector's 10-connection pool filled during short stalls in the first round). Dashed line at 1.
panels.title: DB connections waiting (Hikari pending)

panels.description: Java heap in use per service. A saw-tooth is normal; a rising floor across a long run hints at a leak.
panels.title: JVM heap used

panels.description: Longest garbage-collection pause per service. During a pause the service does nothing, which shows as latency spikes.
panels.title: Longest GC pause

panels.description: CPU used per CCE container (names starting with "cce-"), in cores, from cAdvisor. The k6 container and this monitoring stack are not included. On a laptop everything shares the same cores, so one busy container slows the others.
panels.title: Container CPU (cores)

panels.description: Memory per CCE container, from cAdvisor (what counts against the container's limit).
panels.title: Container memory (working set)

panels.description: Free space on the host root file system, which holds the Docker data root where the Postgres WAL and Kafka logs live (node-exporter). Red below the dashed line: MIN_FREE_DISK_GB = 20 GB, the preflight/cleanup limit. If your Docker data root is on another disk, change the mountpoint in this query.
panels.title: Free disk on / (Docker data root)
Postgres, WAL and replication slots (cleanup lesson: the Debezium slot was lost)

panels.description: Connections to the ccedb database, grouped by state (active, idle, idle in transaction, …), from postgres-exporter. "idle in transaction" that stays up for a whole run holds locks and blocks vacuum: a known problem from the first test round.
panels.title: Postgres connections by state (ccedb)

panels.description: Size of the ccedb database on disk. Grows with every test; cleanup removes rows but the space is reused rather than returned until vacuum.
panels.title: Database size (ccedb)

panels.description: Size of Postgres's write-ahead log directory. It grows while a replication slot (e.g. Debezium for analytics) has not read it; large deletes during cleanup write a lot of WAL. Verify the metric name at first scrape (postgres-exporter wal collector).
panels.title: WAL on disk (pg_wal)

panels.description: Whether each replication slot has a consumer attached (1) or not (0). A slot that is inactive keeps WAL on disk until it is read or lost. Empty when the database has no replication slots (e.g. local-stack without the analytics pipeline). Verify at first scrape.
panels.title: Replication slot active (1 = consumer attached)

panels.description: safe_wal_size: how much more WAL Postgres can write before this slot exceeds max_slot_wal_keep_size and is invalidated ("lost"). In the first round a 27M-row delete did exactly that and analytics stopped syncing. Cleanup stops when this falls below CLEANUP_MIN_SAFE_WAL_GB = 2 GB (dashed line). Verify at first scrape.
panels.title: Replication slot: WAL left before the slot is lost

panels.description: How fast Postgres writes WAL, from the growth of the current WAL position reported with the replication slots (bytes/s). Spikes during load or cleanup explain disk growth and slot pressure. Empty without replication slots. Verify at first scrape.
panels.title: WAL written per second

list.description: k6 label "service": collector, matcher or step-sla. Filters the k6 panels only.
list.label: Service
list.name: service

list.label: Test type
list.name: test_type
